transitions.summary: Functional erratum: the effect gains a hard once-per-turn limit and a delayed self-banish - after returning the card you must banish 1 "Sinister Serpent" from your GY during your opponent's next End Phase. The pre-errata script (pre-errata/c511000818.lua) has neither: its Standby Phase TRIGGER_O carries no SetCountLimit and its operation only does Duel.SendtoHand, while the modern script adds e1:SetCountLimit(1,id) and registers the opponent's-End-Phase Duel.Remove effect on resolution.

rulings_check.difference: Era Sinister Serpent has no once-per-turn limit; the modern card can use its effect only once per turn (hard limit by name). Modern Sinister Serpent, after adding itself to the hand, must banish 1 'Sinister Serpent' from the Graveyard (or Monster Zone) during the opponent's next End Phase; the era card has no such follow-up.

review.notes:
No goat variant exists for this card; the pre-errata variant is the baseline. Its cdb text ('During your Standby Phase, if there is a "Sinister Serpent" in your Graveyard: you can add this card from your Graveyard to your hand.') is not an exact copy of any lineage version - the packet scores it 0.7656 against v0 - it is a modernised paraphrase blending v0's 'if there is a "Sinister Serpent" in your Graveyard' condition with post-PSCT phrasing. Behaviourally it is v0/v1: optional, unlimited, no banish. Recorded as such rather than as a conflict, because the script unambiguously implements the pre-2015 effect. Trailing cosmetic rewordings after the erratum are not recorded as changes: v2 -> v3 (SBAD-EN037, 2019-05-30, Graveyard -> GY) and v3 -> v4 (SBC1-ENH09, 2023-08-24, 'add it' -> 'return it'); v4 is the pinned modern text.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Sinister Serpent). The rulings read support d1 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. Verdicts: [c1] d1 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu; d2 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu.
